url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/getting-started.md

# Getting started

gulp-plugins-hub is a set of gulp plugins, each in its own package, that share one way of working: typed options checked when the plugin is created, hooks that get the file, errors that name the plugin and the file.

## Requirements

* Node.js 22.13 or newer
* gulp 5 (gulp 4 works too)

## Install

Install gulp and the plugins the build needs:

```sh
npm install --save-dev gulp @zilero/gulp-scss-compiler @zilero/gulp-css-squeezer @zilero/gulp-js-squeezer
```

## A first gulpfile

```js
// gulpfile.mjs
import { dest, parallel, src } from 'gulp';
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';
import cssSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

export const styles = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/styles/*.scss', { sourcemaps: true }),
    scssCompiler(),
    cssSqueezer(),
    dest('dist/css', { sourcemaps: '.' })
  );

export const scripts = () =>
  pipeline(src('src/js/*.js', { sourcemaps: true }), jsSqueezer(), dest('dist/js', { sourcemaps: '.' }));

export default parallel(styles, scripts);
```

Tasks return `pipeline(…)` from `node:stream/promises` rather than a `.pipe()` chain, so an error in any step ends the task with that error ([why](/guide/gulp-5#return-pipeline-not-a-pipe-chain)).

```sh
npx gulp
```

Every plugin is a function that takes its options and returns a stream. Each has a default export and a named one:

```js
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';
import { scssCompiler } from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler'; // the same function
```

In a CommonJS gulpfile, use the named export:

```js
// gulpfile.js
const { scssCompiler } = require('@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler');
```

## Options are checked up front

Every option is validated when the plugin is created. A wrong value stops the task before any file is read, and lists every problem:

```text
[10:42:01] 'styles' errored after 3 ms
[10:42:01] Error in plugin "@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer"
Message:
    Invalid options:
    • Unrecognized key: "minfy"
```

## Errors name the file

An error while processing a file is a `PluginError` emitted on the stream, with the plugin name and the file:

```text
[10:42:05] Error in plugin "@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler"
Message:
    Undefined variable.
    ╷
  3 │ .card { color: $brand; }
    │                ^^^^^^
    ╵
Details:
    fileName: /project/src/styles/main.scss
```

In a `watch` task an error stops that run; gulp keeps watching.

## Next

* [Gulp 5 essentials](/guide/gulp-5): binary files, glob order, `pipeline`, TypeScript gulpfiles, source maps.
* [Recipes](/guide/recipes): a complete static site build.
* [Plugins](/plugins/): every plugin and its options.

# Gulp 5 essentials

Gulp 5 changed a few defaults that every build runs into. The plugins handle them, but some need a setting in your gulpfile.

## Binary files need `encoding: false`

Gulp 5 reads every file as UTF-8 text. Images, fonts and other binary files come out corrupted: every byte that is not valid UTF-8 becomes `U+FFFD`. Read them with `encoding: false`:

```js
src('src/images/**', { encoding: false });
src('src/fonts/*.ttf', { encoding: false });
```

[image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer) and [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher) recognize a file read as text and fail with this fix in the message, instead of a decoder error. Plugins that only copy or pack files ([archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator), [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone), [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision)) cannot tell: read binary files with `encoding: false` there too, or the copies are corrupted.

## Glob order is not kept

Gulp 4 emitted the files of `src(['a/*.js', 'b/*.js'])` in the order of the globs. Gulp 5 does not. When order matters, set it in the plugin:

```js
src('src/js/**/*.js').pipe(fileConcat({ name: 'app.js', order: ['vendor/**', 'lib/**'] }));
```

## Source maps without gulp-sourcemaps

`src` and `dest` handle source maps themselves:

```js
src('src/**/*.scss', { sourcemaps: true }) // reads existing maps, starts empty ones
  .pipe(scssCompiler())
  .pipe(cssSqueezer())
  .pipe(dest('dist', { sourcemaps: '.' })); // writes main.css.map next to main.css
```

[scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler), [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer), [js-squeezer](/plugins/js-squeezer) and [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat) produce a map when the file has one, chained to the map before them where the tool supports it. Without `sourcemaps: true` they make none.

## Return `pipeline()`, not a `.pipe()` chain

When a stream in the middle of a `.pipe()` chain fails, gulp never hears the task end: it hangs at "Starting…" and a watcher stops running it. `pipeline` from `node:stream/promises` ends the task with the error:

```js
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';

export const styles = () => pipeline(src('src/scss/*.scss'), scssCompiler(), cssSqueezer(), dest('dist/css'));
```

In a dev task, start the watchers without returning them: a failing task is then reported and the next change runs it again, instead of the error ending the whole dev task.

```js
export const serve = (done) => {
  watch('src/scss/**', styles);
  done();
};
```

## ES modules and TypeScript gulpfiles

The packages are ES modules. Use them from:

* `gulpfile.mjs`, or `gulpfile.js` with `"type": "module"` in package.json: `import`.
* a CommonJS `gulpfile.js`: `const { cssSqueezer } = require('@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer')` (Node.js 22.12+ loads ES modules with `require`).
* `gulpfile.ts`. gulp-cli loads it through a register module it looks for in a fixed order: ts-node, sucrase, @babel/register, esbuild-register, @swc/register. Node's own TypeScript support is not registered for `require`, so without one of them gulp-cli prints an error for each before falling back. Install esbuild-register:

```sh
npm install --save-dev esbuild-register esbuild
```

It compiles the gulpfile and the files it imports on the fly, ES modules included (`"type": "module"`), on every supported Node.js. sucrase does not work with `"type": "module"`, and gulp-cli picks it before esbuild-register when it is installed. The compiled code runs as CommonJS, so top-level `await` is not available in the gulpfile.

The plugins ship their types, and `Vinyl` (the file type hooks receive) is exported by `@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory`.

## Files without contents and streams

`src(…, { read: false })` and directories give files without contents. The plugins pass them through untouched, except the ones that work on paths ([refilename](/plugins/refilename), [file-exclude](/plugins/file-exclude), [conditional](/plugins/conditional), [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone), [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed)).

`src(…, { buffer: false })` gives streamed contents. Only [archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator) accepts them; the others emit `Streaming is not supported`.

# Recipes

## A complete site build

The [example](https://github.com/Zilero232/gulp-plugins-hub/tree/master/apps/example) in the repository is a static site built with every plugin, set up the way a gulp 5 build is in 2026 (TypeScript gulpfile through esbuild-register); CI runs it on the published builds. Its shape:

```text
apps/example/
├── gulpfile.ts          the public tasks: build, release, clean and the default dev task
├── .browserslistrc      the browsers css-squeezer prefixes for
└── gulp/
    ├── config.ts        paths, the --production flag, the version
    ├── tasks/           one task per file: pages, styles, scripts, assets, statics, revision, archive, serve
    └── utils/           the dev server, a `when` helper for steps that run in one mode only
```

```sh
npx gulp                       # build, serve with live reload, rebuild on change
npx gulp build --production    # minified, no source maps, AVIF images
npx gulp release --production  # plus hashed asset names in release/site/ and release/site-v1.0.0.zip
npx gulp --tasks               # the tasks with their descriptions
```

### Configuration

```ts
// gulp/config.ts
import { parseArgs } from 'node:util';

const { values } = parseArgs({ options: { production: { type: 'boolean', default: false } }, strict: false });

export const production = values.production === true || process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production';
```

### Pages

```ts
export const pages = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/pages/**/*.pug'),
    pugCompiler({
      pugOptions: { basedir: 'src', pretty: !production }, // `extends /templates/_layout.pug` resolves from src/
      data: ({ file }) => ({ page: file.stem, year: new Date().getFullYear() })
    }),
    when({ condition: production, then: () => htmlSqueezer({ preset: 'comprehensive' }) }),
    dest('dist')
  );
```

### Styles, with source maps in development

```ts
export const styles = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/scss/**/*.scss', { sourcemaps: !production }),
    scssCompiler(), // partials (_*.scss) are skipped
    cssSqueezer({ minify: production }), // prefixes for .browserslistrc
    dest('dist/css', { sourcemaps: '.' }),
    server.stream({ match: '**/*.css' }) // browser-sync injects the CSS without a reload
  );
```

### Scripts

Bundle the application's modules with a bundler, called from the task; keep gulp plugins for what bundlers do not do:

```ts
const app = () =>
  esbuild.build({ entryPoints: ['src/js/main.js'], outfile: 'dist/js/app.js', bundle: true, minify: production });

// Third-party snippets that stay classic scripts: joined in order, filled in, minified.
const vendor = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/js/vendor/*.js'),
    fileConcat({ name: 'vendor.js', order: 'polyfills.js' }),
    textReplace({ rules: { search: '__ANALYTICS_ID__', replace: process.env.ANALYTICS_ID ?? 'G-EXAMPLE' } }),
    when({ condition: production, then: () => jsSqueezer() }),
    dest('dist/js')
  );

export const scripts = parallel(app, vendor);
```

### Images and fonts in one task

```ts
export const assets = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/{images,fonts}/**', { encoding: false }),
    fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: builtPath }), // encoding is slow: skip what did not change
    conditional({
      handlers: [
        { condition: ({ file }) => isImage(file), handler: () => imageSqueezer({ formats: ['original', 'webp'] }) },
        { condition: ({ file }) => isFont(file), handler: () => fontSwitcher({ formats: ['woff2', 'woff'] }) }
      ]
    }),
    dest('dist')
  );
```

### Release: hashed names and a zip

```ts
const revision = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('dist/**', { encoding: false }),
    assetRevision({ exclude: ['*.html', '*.map', 'robots.txt'], manifest: true }),
    dest('release/site')
  );

const archive = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('release/site/**', { encoding: false }),
    archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip' }),
    refilename({ suffix: `-v${version}` }),
    dest('release')
  );

export const release = series(build, revision, archive);
```

### Dev server

```ts
export const serve = (done) => {
  server.init({ server: 'dist', open: false });

  watch('src/**/*.pug', series(pages, reload));
  watch('src/scss/**', styles);
  watch('src/static/**', series(statics, reload)).on('unlink', (file) => rm(toDist(file), { force: true }));

  done(); // the watchers are not returned: a failing task is reported, and the next change runs it again
};
```

## Incremental builds

* **In one watch session**, `src(globs, { since: lastRun(task) })` reads only the files changed since the task last ran. It suits tasks that copy files one to one.
* **Across runs** (restarting the dev server, running `gulp images` again), [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed) compares with what is already in the output folder. It suits slow work such as image and font encoding.
* Neither suits Sass, Pug or bundles, whose files depend on each other: rebuild their entry points.

## Responsive images

```js
src('src/images/photos/*.jpg', { encoding: false })
  .pipe(imageSqueezer({ formats: ['original', 'webp', 'avif'], widths: [480, 960, 1920] }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/images/photos'));
```

```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/avif" srcset="/images/photos/beach-480w.avif 480w, /images/photos/beach-960w.avif 960w" />
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="/images/photos/beach-480w.webp 480w, /images/photos/beach-960w.webp 960w" />
  <img src="/images/photos/beach-960w.jpg" srcset="/images/photos/beach-480w.jpg 480w" alt="" />
</picture>
```

## Only the glyphs a page needs

```js
src('src/fonts/Display.ttf', { encoding: false })
  .pipe(fontSwitcher({ formats: 'woff2', subset: 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789' }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/fonts'));
```

## A step in one mode only

Plugins are plain functions, so a JavaScript condition decides when the whole stream takes the same path:

```ts
import { PassThrough } from 'node:stream';

const when = ({ condition, then }) => (condition ? then() : new PassThrough({ objectMode: true }));
```

Use [conditional](/plugins/conditional) when the decision depends on each file.

# Writing a plugin

Every plugin in the hub is built with `@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory`. It turns a function that changes one file into a stream that follows the [gulp plugin guidelines](https://github.com/gulpjs/gulp/blob/master/docs/writing-a-plugin/guidelines.md): files without contents pass through, streamed contents are refused, errors become `PluginError`s with the plugin name and file and are emitted rather than thrown, and files leave in the order they came.

```sh
npm install @zilero/gulp-plugin-factory zod
```

## A banner plugin

```ts
import { createPlugin, parseOptions } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
import { z } from 'zod';

const PLUGIN_NAME = 'gulp-banner';

const optionsSchema = z
  .object({ text: z.string().min(1), extensions: z.array(z.string()).default(['.js', '.css']) })
  .strict();

export type BannerOptions = z.input<typeof optionsSchema>;

export const banner = (options: BannerOptions) => {
  // Checked when the plugin is created: invalid options throw a PluginError listing every problem.
  const { text, extensions } = parseOptions({ name: PLUGIN_NAME, schema: optionsSchema, options });

  return createPlugin({
    name: PLUGIN_NAME,
    // Other files pass through untouched.
    filter: (file) => extensions.includes(file.extname),
    transform: (file) => {
      file.contents = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(`${text}\n`), file.contents]);
    }
  });
};
```

## What `transform` returns

| Return            | Effect                                                   |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| nothing           | The file, changed in place, goes on.                     |
| `null`            | The file is dropped.                                     |
| a file            | That file goes on instead.                               |
| an array of files | Each of them goes on, in order: one input, many outputs. |

`transform` may be async; the next file waits for it. To emit files that do not come from one input (a bundle, a manifest), collect in `transform`, return `null`, and `push` the result from `flush`:

```ts
import { createPlugin, Vinyl } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
import path from 'node:path';

export const fileList = () => {
  const names: string[] = [];

  return createPlugin({
    name: 'gulp-file-list',
    transform: (file) => {
      names.push(file.relative);
      return null;
    },
    // A path under the working directory, so `dest('dist')` writes dist/files.txt.
    flush: ({ push }) => push(new Vinyl({ path: path.resolve('files.txt'), contents: Buffer.from(names.join('\n')) }))
  });
};
```

## Files without contents and streams

By default `transform` gets only files with Buffer contents (`accept: 'buffer'`): files without contents pass through and streamed contents emit `Streaming is not supported`. Set `accept: 'any'` to get every file, for plugins that work on paths or handle streams themselves.

## Source maps

When `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })` gave the file a map, pass it to the tool as its input map and store the tool's map:

```ts
import { applySourceMap, createPlugin, getInputSourceMap, toPosixPath } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

createPlugin({
  name: 'gulp-my-minifier',
  transform: async (file) => {
    const result = await minify(file.contents.toString(), {
      filename: toPosixPath(file.relative), // `/` on every OS, or Windows maps get backslashes
      sourceMap: Boolean(file.sourceMap),
      inputSourceMap: getInputSourceMap(file) // undefined when there is nothing to chain
    });

    file.contents = Buffer.from(result.code);
    if (file.sourceMap && result.map) applySourceMap({ file, map: result.map });
  }
});
```

For a tool that cannot take an input map, let `applySourceMap` chain it: `applySourceMap({ file, map, chain: true })`. To chain several inputs into one map yourself (a bundle), `getChainableSourceMap(file)` gives each file's map with absolute sources, ready for `@jridgewell/remapping`.

## Binary files

Call `assertBinaryContents(file)` first in plugins for images, fonts or other binary formats: when gulp 5 read the file as UTF-8 (no `encoding: false`), it throws an error that tells the user how to fix it.

## Options with any schema library

`parseOptions` takes any synchronous [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev): zod 4, valibot, arktype and others. Check callbacks with `isFunction` rather than zod's `z.function()`, which wraps the function and validates its result, and breaks async hooks. `ContentHook` is the type of a hook on a file's text, and `isRelativePathInside` checks paths that must stay inside an output folder:

```ts
import type { ContentHook } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

import { isFunction, isRelativePathInside } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
import { z } from 'zod';

const optionsSchema = z
  .object({
    name: z.string().refine(isRelativePathInside, 'Expected a path inside the output folder'),
    onBeforeWrite: z.custom<ContentHook>(isFunction, 'Expected a function').optional()
  })
  .strict();
```

## Testing

```ts
import { createFile, getContents, runPlugin } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { banner } from './banner';

it('adds the banner to scripts only', async () => {
  const [script, image] = await runPlugin(banner({ text: '/*! hi */' }), [
    createFile({ path: 'app.js', contents: 'run();' }),
    createFile({ path: 'logo.png', contents: 'png' })
  ]);

  expect(getContents(script).toString()).toBe('/*! hi */\nrun();');
  expect(getContents(image).toString()).toBe('png');
});
```

Compare paths with `getRelativePath(file)`, which uses `/` on every OS, so the tests pass on Windows too.

The full API is in the [factory reference](/reference/factory) and the [testing reference](/reference/testing).

# Migrating from 1.x

2.0 rewrites every package for gulp 5 and Node.js 22.13+. The packages keep their names; the options changed where 1.x had bugs or nested everything under `pluginOptions`.

## Everywhere

* **Node.js 22.13+**, ES modules. In a CommonJS gulpfile use the named export: `const { scssCompiler } = require('@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler')`.
* **gulp is no longer a peer dependency**, as the [gulp guidelines](https://github.com/gulpjs/gulp/blob/master/docs/writing-a-plugin/guidelines.md) ask.
* **Hooks are flat and get the file**: `pluginOptions: { onBeforeMinify(content) }` became `onBeforeMinify({ content, file })`.
* **Errors** are `PluginError`s with the plugin name and file, emitted on the stream. Invalid options list every problem instead of printing a box and throwing an empty error.
* **Files without contents** (directories, `read: false`) pass through instead of failing with `File is null`.
* **Files outside a plugin's formats pass through**: the minifiers and compilers only touch their own extensions.
* **Binary files** need `src(globs, { encoding: false })` with gulp 5; image and font plugins say so when they get a file read as text.

## Package by package

| Package              | 1.x                                                                                            | 2.0                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| gulp-plugin-factory  | `GulpPluginFactory({ pluginName, onFile, onFinish })`; `undefined` dropped the file            | `createPlugin({ name, transform, flush })`; nothing returned keeps the file, `null` drops it. Plus `parseOptions`, source map and testing helpers. |
| gulp-refilename      | object only                                                                                    | also a file name string or a function of the path parts                                                                                            |
| gulp-file-exclude    | `patterns` matched as substrings; `size: [min, max]`; `onExclude`                              | `patterns` are globs or RegExps; `size: { min, max }`; `exclude`                                                                                   |
| gulp-conditional     | the condition was checked once, for the whole stream                                           | checked per file, conditions get the file, branches created on first use                                                                           |
| gulp-folder-clone    | `onBeforeCopy`; files passed through unchanged                                                 | copies every file into `dirs`; `keepOriginal`, `onClone`                                                                                           |
| gulp-archive-creator | `format`, `archiveOptions`, `pluginOptions.archiveName`                                        | `name` (format from its extension), `format`, `archiverOptions`, `emptyArchive`, `directories`; tgz                                                |
| gulp-font-switcher   | fontmin; `pluginOptions.format`, `fontOptions.glyph`                                           | harfbuzz subsetting and fontverter, every OpenType table kept (no native build); `formats` (several at once), `subset`, `hinting`, `keepOriginal`  |
| gulp-html-squeezer   | html-minifier-terser, nothing minified without options                                         | html-minifier-next, `preset: 'conservative'` by default                                                                                            |
| gulp-js-squeezer     | `minifyOptions`, no source maps                                                                | `terserOptions`, source maps chained                                                                                                               |
| gulp-pug-compiler    | rendered the file on disk, partials included                                                   | renders the contents; `data`, `extname`, `skipPartials`                                                                                            |
| gulp-scss-compiler   | `scssOptions`; compiled the file on disk (`onBeforeCompile` was ignored), one process per file | `sassOptions`; compiles the contents with one compiler per stream; partials skipped; source maps; `.sass`                                          |

Each plugin page ends with its own migration notes.

## New in 2.0

[css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer), [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer), [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat), [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace), [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision) and [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed).

# Plugins

Every plugin is its own package under the `@zilero` scope: install only what the build uses.

```sh
npm install --save-dev gulp @zilero/gulp-scss-compiler @zilero/gulp-css-squeezer
```

## Compile

| Plugin                                  | Does                                                                | Replaces  |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| [pug-compiler](/plugins/pug-compiler)   | Pug templates to HTML, with data per file; partials are skipped.    | gulp-pug  |
| [scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler) | SCSS and indented Sass to CSS with sass-embedded, source maps kept. | gulp-sass |

## Optimize

| Plugin                                    | Does                                                                           | Replaces                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| [html-squeezer](/plugins/html-squeezer)   | Minifies HTML with html-minifier-next presets.                                 | gulp-htmlmin                      |
| [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer)     | Minifies, prefixes and lowers CSS for your browsers with Lightning CSS.        | gulp-clean-css, gulp-autoprefixer |
| [js-squeezer](/plugins/js-squeezer)       | Minifies JavaScript with terser, source maps chained.                          | gulp-terser, gulp-uglify          |
| [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer) | Optimizes images, converts to WebP and AVIF, resizes for `srcset`, with sharp. | gulp-imagemin, gulp-webp          |
| [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher)   | Converts fonts to woff2, woff, ttf, eot and svg, with glyph subsetting.        | gulp-ttf2woff2, gulp-fontmin      |

## Transform

| Plugin                                      | Does                                                                           | Replaces                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat)         | Joins files into one, in the order you set, with a header and footer.          | gulp-concat, gulp-header   |
| [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace)       | Replaces text with strings, regular expressions or async functions.            | gulp-replace, gulp-header  |
| [refilename](/plugins/refilename)           | Renames files: a name, a prefix or suffix, an extension, a folder, a function. | gulp-rename                |
| [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision)   | Content hashes in asset names, references rewritten, a manifest.               | gulp-rev, gulp-rev-rewrite |
| [archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator) | Packs the stream into a zip, tar or tar.gz archive.                            | gulp-zip, gulp-tar         |

## Route and filter

| Plugin                                | Does                                                                   | Replaces                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| [conditional](/plugins/conditional)   | Sends each file through the first branch whose condition holds for it. | gulp-if                  |
| [file-exclude](/plugins/file-exclude) | Drops files by glob, regular expression, size or predicate.            | gulp-filter, gulp-ignore |
| [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed) | Lets through only the files that changed since the last build.         | gulp-changed, gulp-newer |
| [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone) | Copies every file into extra folders in one pass.                      | gulp-clone               |

All of them are built with the [plugin factory](/guide/writing-plugins), which you can use for your own.

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/pug-compiler.md

# pug-compiler

Renders Pug templates to HTML from the file contents, so earlier plugins can change them. Locals come from an object or a function of each file, includes and `extends` resolve from the file's own path, and partials such as `_layout.pug` are dropped.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-pug-compiler
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import pugCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-pug-compiler';

export const pages = () =>
  src('src/**/*.pug')
    .pipe(pugCompiler({ data: { year: 2026 }, pugOptions: { pretty: true } })) // index.pug → index.html
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

`data` can be a function that returns the locals for each file, the output can have another extension, and `onBeforeCompile` changes the template before pug sees it:

```js
pugCompiler({ data: async ({ file }) => ({ page: file.stem }) }); // front matter, a JSON file next to it, …
pugCompiler({ extname: '.php' }); // index.pug → index.php
pugCompiler({ onBeforeCompile: ({ content }) => content.replaceAll('{{year}}', '2026') });
```

## Options

| Option            | Type                                                | Default   | Description                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pugOptions`      | `Options`                                           | —         | Passed to pug as an object: `pretty`, `doctype`, `filters`, `basedir`, … `filename` is set by the plugin.       |
| `data`            | `object \| ({ file }) => object \| Promise<object>` | —         | Locals for every template, or a function that returns them for each file.                                       |
| `extname`         | `string`                                            | `'.html'` | The extension of the output, with its dot.                                                                      |
| `skipPartials`    | `boolean`                                           | `true`    | Drop files whose name starts with `_` (layouts, mixins, includes) instead of rendering them.                    |
| `onBeforeCompile` | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>`  | —         | Runs on the template source before pug and returns the source to compile. The file still has its own extension. |
| `onAfterCompile`  | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>`  | —         | Runs on the rendered HTML and returns the final HTML. The file already has its new extension.                   |

Unknown keys, an extension without its dot such as `'html'`, a `data` that is neither an object nor a function and a `pugOptions` that is not an object are an error when the plugin is created.

## Notes

* Only `.pug` and `.jade` files are rendered, in any case. Other files, and files without contents (`read: false`), pass through untouched.
* Relative includes and `extends` resolve from the file's path. Absolute ones (`include /templates/_nav.pug`) resolve from `basedir`, which defaults to `file.base`: the folder before the first glob in `src()`.
* With `skipPartials`, partials leave the stream, so they are not written to `dest`; templates still include them from disk.
* No source maps are produced. A file that already has one (`src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`) keeps it, with `sourceMap.file` following the new extension.
* An error from pug, `data` or a hook, such as a template pug cannot compile or render, emits a PluginError with the file path.
* Templates are compiled with `compileDebug: true`, so an error while rendering quotes the lines of the compiled text, the contents as earlier plugins left them, instead of reading the file from disk. Set `pugOptions: { compileDebug: false }` to turn it off.
* The compiler is [pug](https://pugjs.org) 3; its options go through `pugOptions`.

## Migrating from 1.x

* 1.x compiled the file from disk with `compileFile`, ignoring changes made by earlier plugins. Now the file contents are compiled.
* `data` is new: locals as an object or a function of the file.
* `extname` is new; the default stays `.html`.
* Partials (`_*.pug`) are dropped by default; 1.x rendered every `.pug` file, partials included. `skipPartials: false` keeps them.
* `onAfterCompile` moved from `pluginOptions` to the top level and gets `{ content, file }`.
* `onBeforeCompile` is new: it changes the template source before pug.
* `basedir` defaults to `file.base`, so absolute includes work without options.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

# scss-compiler

Compiles SCSS and indented Sass to CSS with the modern Sass compiler (sass-embedded), from the file contents. One compiler process serves each stream, partials are dropped, and the file gets a source map when it had one.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-scss-compiler
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

export const styles = () =>
  src('src/styles/**/*.scss')
    .pipe(scssCompiler({ sassOptions: { style: 'compressed' } })) // main.scss → main.css
    .pipe(dest('dist/css'));
```

With source maps:

```js
export const styles = () =>
  src('src/styles/**/*.scss', { sourcemaps: true })
    .pipe(scssCompiler())
    .pipe(dest('dist/css', { sourcemaps: '.' })); // main.css and main.css.map
```

## Options

| Option            | Type                                               | Default | Description                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sassOptions`     | `StringOptions`                                    | `{}`    | Passed to Sass: `style`, `loadPaths`, `importers`, `functions`, `silenceDeprecations`, … except `url`, `syntax` and the source map options. |
| `skipPartials`    | `boolean`                                          | `true`  | Drop partials (`_variables.scss`) instead of compiling them on their own.                                                                   |
| `onBeforeCompile` | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —       | Runs on the source before Sass and returns the source to compile.                                                                           |
| `onAfterCompile`  | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —       | Runs on the compiled CSS and returns the final CSS. The file is already renamed to `.css`. Source maps do not follow changes made here.     |

Unknown keys, and a `sassOptions` that is not an object, are an error when the plugin is created.

## Notes

* `.scss` files are compiled as SCSS and `.sass` files as indented syntax, in any case; both become `.css`. Other files, plain `.css` included, and files without contents (`read: false`) pass through untouched.
* `@use` and `@import` resolve relative to the file, then from `sassOptions.loadPaths`, then from `file.base`, which is always searched.
* With `skipPartials`, partials leave the stream, so they are not written to `dest`; other files still load them from disk.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, Sass writes a map with the sources included, relative to `file.base`. Without it, no map is made. `sourceMap`, `sourceMapIncludeSources`, `syntax` and `url` come from the file, not from `sassOptions`.
* Each stream gets one Sass compiler. It starts with the first Sass file to compile and stops when the stream ends or is destroyed by an error, so it never outlives the task.
* A compiler that fails to start, for example because the sass-embedded binary for your platform is missing, fails the file that needed it with a PluginError naming its path, and that error ends the stream as any other error does. The start is not retried for later files.
* A Sass error emits a PluginError that points at the stylesheet where it happened, often a partial, and its line. The message is Sass's own, without the `Error:` prefix, and the details leave out Sass's raw span objects. Other errors, from a hook for example, name the file being compiled.
* The compiler is [sass-embedded](https://sass-lang.com/dart-sass/), the Dart Sass compiler; its options go through `sassOptions`.

## Migrating from 1.x

* `scssOptions` is renamed to `sassOptions`; `url`, `syntax` and `sourceMap` are no longer options because they come from the file.
* 1.x compiled the file from disk, so the result of `onBeforeCompile` was ignored. Now the file contents are compiled, including changes from earlier plugins and from the hook.
* One sass-embedded compiler serves each stream instead of a Sass process per file, and it is stopped at the end or on an error.
* `.sass` files with the indented syntax are supported.
* Partials are dropped by default; 1.x compiled them as well. `skipPartials: false` keeps them.
* Source maps are applied when the file has one; 1.x applied none.
* The hooks moved from `pluginOptions` to the top level and get `{ content, file }`. `onAfterCompile` sees the file already renamed to `.css`.
* Errors are prefixed with `@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler`; 1.x said `GulpScssSqueezer`.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

# html-squeezer

Minifies HTML with html-minifier-next, starting from one of its presets: comments and redundant attributes go, and the `comprehensive` preset also minifies inline CSS, JavaScript and SVG. Other files pass through.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-html-squeezer
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import htmlSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-html-squeezer';

export const html = () =>
  src('dist/**/*.html')
    .pipe(htmlSqueezer({ preset: 'comprehensive' }))
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

Options from `htmlMinifierOptions` are applied over the preset, and the hooks change the markup around the minifier:

```js
htmlSqueezer({ preset: 'comprehensive', htmlMinifierOptions: { removeAttributeQuotes: false } }); // keep quotes
htmlSqueezer({ preset: false, htmlMinifierOptions: { removeComments: true } }); // only what you list
htmlSqueezer({ onAfterMinify: ({ content, file }) => `<!-- ${file.basename} -->\n${content}` });
```

## Options

| Option                | Type                                               | Default          | Description                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `preset`              | `'conservative' \| 'comprehensive' \| false`       | `'conservative'` | The html-minifier-next preset to start from. `conservative` is safe for any page, `comprehensive` gives the smallest output, `false` none. |
| `htmlMinifierOptions` | `MinifierOptions`                                  | —                | html-minifier-next options as an object, applied over the preset.                                                                          |
| `onBeforeMinify`      | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —                | Runs on the markup before minification and returns the markup to minify.                                                                   |
| `onAfterMinify`       | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —                | Runs on the minified markup and returns the final markup.                                                                                  |

Unknown keys, an unknown preset and an `htmlMinifierOptions` that is not an object are an error when the plugin is created.

## Notes

* Only `.html` and `.htm` files are minified, in any case (`INDEX.HTML` too). Other files, and files without contents (`read: false`), pass through untouched.
* `.xhtml` files pass through as well: the presets drop closing slashes and attribute values, which XHTML served as XML does not allow.
* Source maps are not updated: HTML has none to follow.
* An error from the minifier or a hook, such as markup it cannot parse, emits a PluginError with the file path.
* The minifier is [html-minifier-next](https://github.com/j9t/html-minifier-next); every one of its options goes through `htmlMinifierOptions`.

## Migrating from 1.x

* html-minifier-terser 7, which is no longer maintained, is replaced by html-minifier-next 9.
* 1.x had no defaults, so without options it barely minified anything. Now the `conservative` preset applies by default; `preset: false` with your own `htmlMinifierOptions` gets the old behavior.
* The hooks moved from `pluginOptions` to the top level and get `{ content, file }` instead of the content alone.
* Only HTML files are processed; 1.x ran the minifier on every file in the stream.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/css-squeezer.md

# css-squeezer

Minifies CSS, adds the vendor prefixes your browsers need and lowers modern syntax (nesting, `oklch()`, …) with Lightning CSS: clean-css and autoprefixer in one pass. When the file has a source map, the new map is chained to it.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-css-squeezer
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import cssSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer';

export const styles = () =>
  src('dist/css/**/*.css')
    .pipe(cssSqueezer({ targets: '> 0.5%, last 2 versions, not dead' }))
    .pipe(dest('dist/css'));
```

With source maps, after a Sass compiler for example:

```js
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

export const styles = () =>
  src('src/styles/**/*.scss', { sourcemaps: true })
    .pipe(scssCompiler())
    .pipe(cssSqueezer())
    .pipe(dest('dist/css', { sourcemaps: '.' })); // the map points to the .scss sources
```

## Options

| Option                | Type                                               | Default                                      | Description                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `targets`             | `string \| string[]`                               | the browserslist config nearest to each file | The browsers to support, as a browserslist query: `'defaults'`, `['> 0.5%', 'not dead']`. See below.            |
| `minify`              | `boolean`                                          | `true`                                       | Minify the output. `false` only adds prefixes and lowers syntax.                                                |
| `lightningcssOptions` | `TransformOptions`                                 | —                                            | Other Lightning CSS options, as an object: `drafts`, `nonStandard`, `errorRecovery`, `cssModules`, `visitor`, … |
| `onBeforeMinify`      | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —                                            | Runs on the source before Lightning CSS and returns the stylesheet to process.                                  |
| `onAfterMinify`       | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —                                            | Runs on the output and returns the final stylesheet. Source maps do not follow changes made here.               |

Unknown keys, an empty `targets` query and a `lightningcssOptions` that is not an object are an error when the plugin is created. So is a query browserslist does not understand, with `Invalid targets: …` and browserslist's message, before any file is read.

### Targets

The browsers come from the first of these that exists:

1. The `targets` option.
2. The browserslist config nearest to the file: a `.browserslistrc` or the `browserslist` key of a `package.json`, looked up from the file's folder upward. It is resolved once per folder: files in the same folder share the result.
3. browserslist's defaults.

Prefixes are added and syntax is lowered only as far as those browsers need: for `chrome 130` nesting stays as it is, for `safari 10` it is flattened and `user-select` gets its `-webkit-` prefix.

## Notes

* Only `.css` files are processed, in any case. Other files, and files without contents (`read: false`), pass through untouched.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, Lightning CSS writes a map, and the plugin chains it to the map the file already had, such as the one from a Sass compiler: the result points to the `.scss` sources only, without the intermediate CSS file as an extra source. Source names use `/` on every OS.
* A syntax error from Lightning CSS emits a PluginError with the file path, `lineNumber` set and the message suffixed with where it is: `Unexpected end of input (line 3, column 1)`. Other errors from Lightning CSS or a hook emit a PluginError with the file path. `lightningcssOptions: { errorRecovery: true }` skips invalid rules instead.
* The tool is [Lightning CSS](https://lightningcss.dev); its options go through `lightningcssOptions`, except `code`, `filename`, `sourceMap`, `minify` and `targets`, which the plugin sets, and `inputSourceMap`, since the plugin chains the input map itself.

---

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/js-squeezer.md

# js-squeezer

Minifies JavaScript with terser. When the file has a source map, the new map is chained to it, so the minified code still points to the original sources. Other files pass through.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-js-squeezer
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';

export const scripts = () =>
  src('src/js/**/*.js')
    .pipe(jsSqueezer({ terserOptions: { module: true, compress: { drop_console: true } } }))
    .pipe(dest('dist/js'));
```

With source maps:

```js
export const scripts = () =>
  src('src/js/**/*.js', { sourcemaps: true })
    .pipe(jsSqueezer())
    .pipe(dest('dist/js', { sourcemaps: '.' })); // app.js and app.js.map
```

## Options

| Option           | Type                                               | Default | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `terserOptions`  | `Omit<MinifyOptions, 'sourceMap'>`                 | `{}`    | Passed to terser's `minify`: `compress`, `mangle`, `format`, `module`, … Not `sourceMap`: the plugin sets it from the file. |
| `onBeforeMinify` | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —       | Runs on the source before terser and returns the code to minify.                                                            |
| `onAfterMinify`  | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>` | —       | Runs on terser's output and returns the final code. Source maps do not follow changes made here.                            |

Unknown keys, and a `terserOptions` that is not an object, are an error when the plugin is created.

## Notes

* Only `.js`, `.mjs` and `.cjs` files are minified, in any case. Other files, and files without contents (`read: false`), pass through untouched.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, terser writes a map with the sources included and chains it to the map the file already had (from a bundler or an earlier plugin). `dest(…, { sourcemaps: '.' })` writes it next to the file. Without a map on the file, none is made.
* Source names in the map are relative to `file.base` and use `/` on every OS, Windows included.
* An error from terser or a hook, such as code terser cannot parse, emits a PluginError with the file path.
* The minifier is [terser](https://terser.org); its options go through `terserOptions`, except `sourceMap`. Set `module: true` for ES modules.

## Migrating from 1.x

* `minifyOptions` is renamed to `terserOptions`.
* The hooks moved from `pluginOptions` to the top level and get `{ content, file }` instead of the content alone.
* Source maps are new: 1.x produced none.
* Only JavaScript files are processed; 1.x ran terser on every file in the stream.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/image-squeezer.md

# image-squeezer

Optimizes JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF and TIFF images with [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com), converts them to WebP, AVIF, JPEG or PNG and resizes them to several widths for `srcset`. Photos are turned upright from the orientation stored in their metadata. SVG and other files pass through.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-image-squeezer
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import imageSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-image-squeezer';

export const images = () =>
  src('src/images/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(imageSqueezer({ formats: ['original', 'webp', 'avif'], widths: [640, 1280] }))
    // hero.jpg → hero-640w.jpg, hero-640w.webp, hero-640w.avif, hero-1280w.jpg, …
    .pipe(dest('dist/images'));
```

Images are binary: read them with `encoding: false`. Gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default, which corrupts binary data.

Without options, every image is optimized in its own format and keeps its name:

```js
imageSqueezer();
imageSqueezer({ formats: 'webp', quality: 70 });
imageSqueezer({ quality: { webp: 75, avif: 50 }, encoderOptions: { png: { palette: true } } });
```

## Options

| Option           | Type                 | Default          | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | -------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formats`        | `Format \| Format[]` | `'original'`     | `'original'`, `'webp'`, `'avif'`, `'jpeg'` or `'png'`, or a list of them. `'original'` re-encodes in the source's own format. Each image becomes one file per format and width. |
| `widths`         | `number[]`           | keep the size    | Widths in pixels: `hero.jpg` becomes `hero-640w.jpg`, `hero-1280w.jpg`, … Images are never enlarged.                                                                            |
| `quality`        | `number \| object`   | encoder defaults | 1 to 100 for every lossy encoder, or per encoder: `{ jpeg, webp, avif, tiff }`. PNG and GIF ignore it.                                                                          |
| `encoderOptions` | `object`             | none             | sharp options per encoder (`jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `avif`, `gif`, `tiff`), merged over the defaults and `quality`.                                                               |
| `keepSmaller`    | `boolean`            | `true`           | Keep the source when re-encoding it in its own format made it bigger.                                                                                                           |

Unknown keys, a quality outside 1–100 and empty `formats` or `widths` lists are an error when the plugin is created.

### Encoder defaults

Tuned for the web: visually lossless, and AVIF at a moderate effort because it encodes slowly.

| Encoder | Settings                            |
| ------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `jpeg`  | `quality: 80`, `mozjpeg: true`      |
| `png`   | `compressionLevel: 9`, `effort: 10` |
| `webp`  | `quality: 80`, `effort: 5`          |
| `avif`  | `quality: 55`, `effort: 4`          |
| `gif`   | `effort: 10`                        |
| `tiff`  | `quality: 80`                       |

`quality` overrides the default quality, and `encoderOptions` override both.

## Notes

* Files ending in `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.webp`, `.avif`, `.gif`, `.tif` and `.tiff` (in any case) are processed. SVG, every other file and files without contents pass through untouched.

* Outputs are ordered by width, then by the order of `formats`. A converted file takes the format's extension (`.webp`, `.avif`, `.jpg`, `.png`); `'original'` keeps the source extension.

* A width larger than the image keeps the image's size, but the name still carries the width asked for: a 400 px image with `widths: [800]` becomes `photo-800w.png` at 400 px.

* `keepSmaller` applies only to `'original'` without `widths`: the source is emitted unchanged when the re-encoded file is not smaller. Converted and resized files are always the encoder's output.

* Photos are turned upright from the orientation stored in their metadata before resizing, so `widths` apply to the upright image.

* Asking for `'original'` and the source's own format (`formats: ['original', 'png']` on a `.png`) writes the file once, as `'original'`, with the source extension.

* Pages and frames are kept only between formats that can hold them:

  | Source               | Output              | Keeps               |
  | -------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------- |
  | animated GIF or WebP | GIF or WebP         | every frame         |
  | multi-page TIFF      | TIFF (`'original'`) | every page          |
  | anything else        | any other format    | the first page only |

* JPEG has no transparency: transparent pixels become white in JPEG output.

* An image read as UTF-8 text fails with an error that names the file and says to use `src(globs, { encoding: false })`.

* sharp ships prebuilt native binaries per platform as optional dependencies. An install that skips optional dependencies (`--no-optional`, `--omit=optional`) leaves them out and sharp fails to load.

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/font-switcher.md
---
# font-switcher

Converts fonts from `ttf`, `otf`, `woff`, `woff2`, `eot` and SVG fonts into `woff2`, `woff`, `ttf`, `eot` and `svg`, into one format or several at once, and can keep only the glyphs you use. Subsetting is done by [subset-font](https://github.com/papandreou/subset-font) (hb-subset) and keeps ligatures, kerning and the other OpenType features. All WebAssembly: there is no native build to install.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-font-switcher
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import fontSwitcher from '@zilero/gulp-font-switcher';

export const fonts = () =>
  src('src/fonts/*.{ttf,otf}', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(fontSwitcher({ formats: ['woff2', 'woff'] })) // Inter.ttf → Inter.woff2, Inter.woff
    .pipe(dest('dist/fonts'));
```

Fonts are binary: read them with `encoding: false`. Gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default, which corrupts binary data.

To ship only the characters a site uses, pass them as `subset`:

```js
fontSwitcher({ formats: 'woff2', subset: 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 .,!?' });
fontSwitcher({ formats: 'woff2', subset: [0x20, 0x41, 0x42, 0x2014] }); // Unicode code points
```

## Options

| Option         | Type                 | Default      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `formats`      | `Format \| Format[]` | *(required)* | `'woff2'`, `'woff'`, `'ttf'`, `'eot'` or `'svg'`, or a list of them. Each font becomes one file per format.                                                                                                  |
| `subset`       | `string \| number[]` | every glyph  | Keep only these glyphs: the characters of a string, or Unicode code points. The kept glyphs keep their OpenType features.                                                                                    |
| `hinting`      | `boolean`            | `true`       | Keep the hinting instructions (sharper text on low-resolution screens) when subsetting and in the rebuilt formats (`ttf` from CFF, `eot`, `svg`). `woff2`, `woff` and TrueType `ttf` keep the font as it is. |
| `keepOriginal` | `boolean`            | `false`      | Emit the source font as well as the converted ones.                                                                                                                                                          |

`otf` is read but not written. Unknown keys, an empty `formats` list, an empty `subset` string and an empty list of code points are an error when the plugin is created. So is a code point that is not an integer from 0 to U+10FFFF (`0x10FFFF`), such as `0x110000` (`Expected a Unicode code point`). A format listed twice is written once.

## Output formats

| Output                 | Made by                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `woff2`, `woff`        | The same font in another container, every table kept ([container converter](https://github.com/papandreou/fontverter)).                               |
| `ttf` from TrueType    | The font as it is, every table kept.                                                                                                                  |
| `ttf` from CFF (`otf`) | Rebuilt by [fonteditor-core](https://github.com/kekee000/fonteditor-core), which turns the outlines into TrueType without the OpenType layout tables. |
| `eot`, `svg`           | Rebuilt by fonteditor-core, without the OpenType layout tables (ligatures, kerning).                                                                  |

`eot` and SVG-font inputs are read through fonteditor-core, which rebuilds them from their glyphs as TrueType, so their outputs have no OpenType layout tables either. `ttf`, `otf`, `woff` and `woff2` inputs are unpacked as they are.

## Notes

* Files ending in `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff`, `.woff2` and `.eot` (in any case) are converted, and `.svg` files that are SVG fonts (a `<font>` element inside). Every other file passes through untouched, SVG images included, and so do files without contents. An SVG with only a `<font-face>` element and no `<font>` is not a font and passes through.
* The output keeps the name and folder and takes the format's extension: `fonts/Inter.ttf` becomes `fonts/Inter.woff2`. Outputs follow the order of `formats`; with `keepOriginal`, the source comes first and is not converted to its own format again, so `keepOriginal` with `formats: ['ttf', 'woff2']` on a `.ttf` emits the source and a woff2.
* With `keepOriginal` and `subset`, a requested format equal to the source's is subset and takes the source's path: `keepOriginal` with `formats: ['ttf', 'woff2']` and a `subset` on a `.ttf` emits a subset ttf and a subset woff2, not the full source as well. When the source's format is not requested, the source is emitted as it is, not subset.
* `hinting: false` drops the hinting instructions when subsetting and in the rebuilt formats (`ttf` from CFF, `eot`, `svg`); without `subset`, `woff2`, `woff` and TrueType `ttf` outputs keep the font, hinting included.
* A binary font read as UTF-8 text fails with an error that names the file and says to use `src(globs, { encoding: false })`.
* An encoder that produces an empty file is an error, never an empty output.
* A broken font emits a PluginError with the file name.

## Migrating from 1.x

* fontmin and fonteditor-core's lossy writing were replaced: subsetting by subset-font and container conversion keep every table of the font, ligatures and kerning included. Conversion is all WebAssembly, with no native dependencies.
* `{ pluginOptions: { format }, fontOptions: { glyph } }` becomes flat options: `format` is now `formats`, which takes one format or several, and `glyph.text` is now `subset`, which also takes code points.
* `hinting` is a top-level option, `true` by default. There is no `kerning` option: kerning is always kept in `woff2`, `woff` and TrueType `ttf` outputs.
* `keepOriginal` (default `false`) is new.
* `woff`, `woff2` and `eot` fonts are read too, not only `ttf`, `otf` and `svg`.
* Other files pass through instead of throwing an error.

```js
// 1.x
fontSwitcher({ pluginOptions: { format: 'woff2' }, fontOptions: { glyph: { text: 'abc' } } });
// 2.0
fontSwitcher({ formats: 'woff2', subset: 'abc' });
```

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/file-concat.md
---
# file-concat

Joins every file of the stream into one, with a separator between files, an optional header and footer, and an order you set with globs. When any input has a source map, the result gets one that chains every input's own map, so it points at the original sources.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-file-concat
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import fileConcat from '@zilero/gulp-file-concat';

export const scripts = () =>
  src('src/js/**/*.js', { sourcemaps: true })
    .pipe(
      fileConcat({
        name: 'bundle.js',
        order: ['vendor/**', '**'], // vendor files first, then the rest
        separator: ';\n',
        header: '/*! My site */\n'
      })
    )
    .pipe(dest('dist/js', { sourcemaps: '.' }));
```

The header and footer can be functions of the concatenated files, sync or async:

```js
fileConcat({ name: 'app.css', header: ({ files }) => `/* ${files.length} files */\n` });
```

## Options

| Option      | Type                 | Default      | Description                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | -------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`      | `string`             | *(required)* | The result's path relative to the output folder: `app.js`, `vendor/bundle.css`. Must stay inside the output folder (not absolute, no leading `..`).             |
| `order`     | `string \| string[]` | stream order | One glob or several, matched against the path relative to each file's `file.base`: files matching the first glob come first, then the second, …, then the rest. |
| `separator` | `string`             | `'\n'`       | Put between two files.                                                                                                                                          |
| `header`    | `string \| function` | none         | Added once at the start. A function gets `{ files }` (in their final order) and returns the text or a promise of it.                                            |
| `footer`    | `string \| function` | none         | Added once at the end. Same forms as `header`.                                                                                                                  |

Unknown keys, an empty `order` list and an empty glob are an error when the plugin is created.

## Notes

* Gulp 5 no longer keeps the order of the globs given to `src`: `src(['vendor/*.js', 'app/*.js'])` can emit `app` files first. Use `order` when the order matters.
* The sort is stable: files matching the same glob, and files matching none, keep their stream order. Globs match dot files too.
* Every file with contents is held until the stream ends and replaced by the single result; files without contents (directories, `read: false`) pass through. An empty stream emits nothing.
* The result is placed under the `base` and `cwd` of the first file in the stream, so `dest` writes it at `name` inside the output folder. Files from different bases are joined too.
* A source map is created when any input has one (`src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`). It chains each input's own map, so it points at the original sources (a compiled `js/a.js` maps back to `ts/a.ts`), with their contents included. Inputs without a map of their own are sources themselves. Source names are relative to the base of the first file: `../app/index.js` for a file from another base. This holds when `name` contains a folder too: with `name: 'vendor/bundle.js'` the sources stay relative to the base and the input maps are still chained, so `dest(…, { sourcemaps: '.' })` writes a map that resolves.
* An empty header or footer adds nothing.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/text-replace.md
---
# text-replace

Replaces text in every file with strings or regular expressions, with sync or async replacer functions that see the match and the file, then adds an optional header and footer. Source maps follow every change. Binary files are left alone. It replaces both gulp-replace and gulp-header/gulp-footer.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-text-replace
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import textReplace from '@zilero/gulp-text-replace';

const version = '2.0.0';

export const release = () =>
  src('dist/**/*.{html,js}')
    .pipe(
      textReplace({
        rules: [
          { search: '__VERSION__', replace: version },
          { search: /https?:\/\/localhost:\d+/g, replace: 'https://example.com' }
        ],
        header: ({ file }) => `/*! ${file.relative} | MIT */\n`
      })
    )
    .pipe(dest('release'));
```

A replacer function gets the match, its groups, its offset and the file, and can be async:

```js
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

textReplace({
  rules: {
    search: /<!--\s*include:(?<name>[\w.-]+)\s*-->/g,
    replace: async ({ namedGroups }) => readFile(`src/partials/${namedGroups.name}`, 'utf8')
  }
});
```

## Options

| Option       | Type                           | Default | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`      | `ReplaceRule \| ReplaceRule[]` | none    | One rule or several, applied in order: each sees the result of the previous one.                                       |
| `header`     | `string \| function`           | none    | Added at the start of every file, after the rules. A function gets `{ file }` and returns the text or a promise of it. |
| `footer`     | `string \| function`           | none    | Added at the end of every file, after the rules. Same forms as `header`.                                               |
| `skipBinary` | `boolean`                      | `true`  | Leave files that contain a NUL byte (images, fonts, archives) untouched.                                               |

At least one of `rules`, `header` or `footer` is required ("Set at least one of rules, header or footer"). Unknown keys, an empty `rules` list and an empty search string are an error when the plugin is created.

### A rule

| Key       | Type                 | Description                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `search`  | `string \| RegExp`   | A string matches literally, everywhere it occurs. A RegExp follows JavaScript: add `g` for every match.                              |
| `replace` | `string \| function` | The replacement. With a RegExp, a string's `$` patterns are filled in (see below). A function returns the replacement for one match. |

The replacer function gets one object:

| Field         | Description                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `match`       | The matched text.                                                |
| `groups`      | Capture groups of a RegExp, in order; empty for a string search. |
| `namedGroups` | Named capture groups.                                            |
| `offset`      | Where the match starts in the contents.                          |
| `file`        | The Vinyl file.                                                  |

## Notes

* A string search with a string replacement is literal on both sides: `$&`, `$1` and other `$` patterns are inserted as written, not interpreted.
* With a RegExp, a string replacement fills in `$&`, `$1`…`$99`, `$<name>`, `` $` ``, `$'` and `$$` the way `String.prototype.replace` does. `$<name>` for a group the RegExp does not have is empty, even for a name such as `toString` (there is no prototype lookup); in a RegExp without named groups it stays as written.
* A RegExp without `g` replaces the first match only, as `String.prototype.replace` does; with a replacer function too. A global or sticky RegExp starts from the beginning in every file: its `lastIndex` never carries over.
* Empty matches are replaced too: `/^/gm` with `'> '` quotes every line.
* A file counts as binary when its first 8000 bytes contain a NUL byte, the check git makes. With `skipBinary: false`, binary files are decoded as UTF-8 like the others.
* Files without contents pass through; streamed contents (`buffer: false`) emit an error.
* Replacers run one match at a time, in order, so an async replacer can rely on the order of the calls.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, `file.sourceMap` follows every change (replacements, header, footer) and chains into the file's existing map, so it still points at the original text. When the file is the first step after `src`, the original text (`sourcesContent`) of the map `src` started is kept.
* Source maps are built only for files that have one: files without `file.sourceMap` skip that work.

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/refilename.md
---
# refilename

Renames every file in the stream: a new name, a prefix or suffix, another extension or folder, or whatever a function of the path returns. Source maps follow the new name.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-refilename
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import refilename from '@zilero/gulp-refilename';

export const scripts = () =>
  src('src/js/*.js')
    .pipe(refilename({ suffix: '.min' })) // app.js → app.min.js
    .pipe(dest('dist/js'));
```

The option is one of three things:

```js
refilename('bundle.js'); // a new file name, the folder stays
refilename({ prefix: 'v2-', extname: '.mjs' }); // changes to the parts of the path
refilename(({ parts, file }) => ({ dirname: 'styles', stem: parts.stem.toLowerCase() })); // a function
```

## Options

The option is checked when the plugin is created; an invalid one throws a `PluginError` that lists every problem.

### A string

The new file name with its extension. The file stays in its folder: `js/app.js` with `'bundle.js'` becomes `js/bundle.js`. The string must be a file name without a folder: `'sub/app.js'` or `'sub\\app.js'` is an error (`Expected a file name without a folder; use { dirname } to move files`), and so is an empty string, `'.'` or `'..'` (`Expected a file name`).

### An object

| Option    | Type     | Default | Description                                                                                          |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dirname` | `string` | none    | New folder, relative to `file.base`. `'.'` moves the file to the base. It must stay inside the base. |
| `stem`    | `string` | none    | New name without the extension. Must not be empty, `.` or `..`.                                      |
| `extname` | `string` | none    | New extension. The leading dot is optional; `''` removes the extension.                              |
| `prefix`  | `string` | none    | Added before the stem.                                                                               |
| `suffix`  | `string` | none    | Added after the stem, before the extension.                                                          |

What the object leaves out stays as it was. Unknown keys are an error, so a typo such as `stemm` fails when the plugin is created instead of doing nothing.

These values are rejected:

* `dirname` that is absolute or leaves the base, such as `'../out'` (`Expected a folder inside the base`);
* an empty `stem`, or a `stem` of `'.'` or `'..'` (`Expected a file name without the extension`);
* a `stem`, `prefix` or `suffix` with `/` or `\` (`Expected part of a file name, without / or \`), since a folder separator would move the file;
* an `extname` that is not an extension, such as `'.'`, `'..js'` or one with a slash (`Expected an extension, like .js or js, or an empty string`).

### A function

`({ parts, file }) => Partial<PathParts>` gets the current parts and the Vinyl file and returns the parts to change. It may be async and return a promise. What it leaves out, or returns as `undefined`, stays as it was. A returned `extname` without the leading dot gets one.

```js
import { stat } from 'node:fs/promises';

refilename(async ({ parts, file }) => {
  const { mtime } = await stat(file.path);

  return { stem: `${parts.stem}-${mtime.getTime()}` }; // app.js → app-1730000000000.js
});

refilename(({ parts }) => ({ dirname: parts.dirname === '.' ? 'root' : undefined })); // only files in the base move
```

| Part      | Example for `css/theme.min.css` |
| --------- | ------------------------------- |
| `dirname` | `css`                           |
| `stem`    | `theme.min`                     |
| `extname` | `.css`                          |

The function's result is checked like the same keys of the object option: a `dirname` outside the base, an empty `stem`, a `stem` of `.` or `..` or with `/` or `\`, or an invalid `extname` emits an error (`The rename function returned invalid parts: …`). Other keys it returns are ignored.

If the new path would still end up outside `file.base`, the file emits an error instead of being renamed (`… would be renamed outside its base: …`).

## Types

The package exports `RefilenameOptions` (the option), `RenameObject` (the object form), `PathParts` (`dirname`, `stem`, `extname`), `RenameFunction` and `RenameInput` (`{ parts, file }`, what the function gets).

## Notes

* Every file is renamed, including files without contents (`read: false`), streamed contents and directories.
* The stem is everything before the **last** extension: a suffix on `theme.min.css` gives `theme.min.suffix.css`.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, `file.sourceMap.file` is updated, so `dest(…, { sourcemaps: '.' })` writes the map under the new name.

## Migrating from 1.x

* A string option now works; it was rejected before.
* A function option is new.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.
