---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/asset-revision.md
---
# asset-revision

Cache-busting for a whole site: renames assets after a hash of their contents (`main.css` → `main-3f2a9c1b7d.css`), rewrites the references to them in HTML, CSS, JavaScript and other text files, and can write a manifest. Pages and source maps keep their names.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-asset-revision
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import assetRevision from '@zilero/gulp-asset-revision';

export const revision = () =>
  src('build/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(assetRevision({ manifest: true }))
    .pipe(dest('release'));
```

Read with `encoding: false` so images and fonts stay intact: gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default, which corrupts binary data. Text files are still rewritten.

To keep more files under their own names, list them with the defaults, because a given `exclude` replaces the default list:

```js
assetRevision({ exclude: ['*.html', '*.htm', '*.map', 'robots.txt', 'favicon.ico'] });
```

## Options

| Option       | Type                           | Default                        | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hashLength` | `number`                       | `10`                           | Characters of the SHA-256 hash added to names, from 4 to 64.                                                                                           |
| `exclude`    | `string[]`                     | `['*.html', '*.htm', '*.map']` | Globs of files that keep their names; references inside them are still rewritten. Case does not matter. Replaces the default list.                     |
| `rewrite`    | `string[] \| false`            | see below                      | Extensions (with the dot) of text files whose references are rewritten, or `false` to only rename.                                                     |
| `manifest`   | `boolean \| { path?: string }` | `false`                        | Emit a JSON manifest of original to revised paths. `true` writes `rev-manifest.json`; `path` is relative to the output folder and must stay inside it. |

The default `rewrite` list is `.html`, `.htm`, `.css`, `.svg`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.json`, `.webmanifest`, `.xml` and `.txt`. Unknown keys are an error when the plugin is created.

A glob without a slash matches the file name in any folder (`*.map` matches `js/app.js.map`); a glob with a slash matches the whole path relative to `file.base` (`img/**`). Dot files match too, and case is ignored: `*.html` matches `INDEX.HTML`.

## Hashing

The hash is the first `hashLength` hex characters of the SHA-256 of the file's contents, added before the extension: `css/main.css` becomes `css/main-3f2a9c1b7d.css`.

A file's hash covers its rewritten references, so a change to an image also changes the names of the stylesheets and scripts that use it. Each text file in the `rewrite` list is scanned once for references to the other assets, and the assets are hashed in that reference graph's topological order: every file after the assets it references, whatever the stream order. So CSS pointing at SVG, CSS importing CSS (`@import`) and JS importing JS are all covered; files that do not depend on each other keep their stream order.

Files on a reference cycle (`a.js` imports `b.js`, which imports `a.js`), the files that depend on them, and files that reference themselves (`new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url)` in `worker.js`) cannot get a hash that covers their own new name, so they keep their names and every reference to them stays valid; only their cache-busting is lost. They are not in the manifest.

Excluded files (pages, maps) and files on a cycle are rewritten last, with every revised name known.

## Rewritten references

References resolve the way a browser does, and a rewritten reference is written the same way as before:

| Form          | Example in `css/main.css` | Resolved from                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| root-relative | `/img/logo.png`           | the base                                                  |
| with `../`    | `../img/logo.png`         | the referencing file                                      |
| with `./`     | `./img/logo.png`          | the referencing file                                      |
| bare          | `img/logo.png`            | the referencing file when that file exists, else the base |

A reference starts at the start of the text or after a quote, a backtick, `(`, `=`, `,` or whitespace, optionally followed by `/` or `./`. It ends at the end of the text or before a quote, a backtick, whitespace, `)`, `,`, `;`, `?`, `#`, `\`, `<`, `>` or `}`. So:

* quoted and unquoted forms both work: `url(img/logo.png)`, `src="img/logo.png"`, and unquoted attributes in minified HTML such as `href=/css/main.css>`;
* query strings and hashes are kept: `img/logo.png?v=1` becomes `img/logo-3f2a9c1b7d.png?v=1`;
* lookalikes are left alone: `other/img/logo.png`, `img/logo.png.bak`, `https://cdn.example.com/img/logo.png`;
* a bare reference that reads the same relative to the file and relative to the base (`img/a.png` in `css/main.css`, with both `css/img/a.png` and `img/a.png` in the stream) points at the asset next to the file, as in a browser; falling back to the base covers pages at the root and scripts that build URLs;
* references to excluded files (`about.html`) are left as they are, since those files keep their names.
* a reference resolves to the file a browser would load even when that file is excluded: with an excluded `blog/logo.png` next to `blog/index.html`, `src="logo.png"` in that page stays as it is rather than pointing at a revised root `logo.png`.

## Manifest

With `manifest`, one more file is emitted after the others: a JSON object of original to revised paths, both relative to the base with `/` separators. Only renamed files are listed.

```json
{
  "img/logo.png": "img/logo-9a1f3c0b2e.png",
  "css/main.css": "css/main-3f2a9c1b7d.css"
}
```

## Notes

* Every file with contents is held until the stream ends, then all of them are emitted together in their original order. Pass the whole site through one call, typically from a build folder into a release folder: references to an asset that goes through another stream are not rewritten.
* Files without contents (directories, `read: false`) pass through at once. An empty stream emits nothing, not even the manifest.
* Extensions are compared in lowercase, in the files and in `rewrite`: `.CSS` files are rewritten like `.css` ones.
* References are rewritten in place: the contents of a renamed text file are those after rewriting.
* A renamed file's `sourceMap.file` follows its new name, so `dest(…, { sourcemaps: '.' })` writes the map for the revised file.

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/archive-creator.md
---
# archive-creator

Packs every file of the stream into one zip, tar or tar.gz archive with archiver and emits only the archive. Entries keep their paths relative to `file.base`, and their modification time and mode when the files came from disk.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-archive-creator
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import archiveCreator from '@zilero/gulp-archive-creator';

export const release = () =>
  src('dist/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip' }))
    .pipe(dest('releases'));
```

The format comes from the name, or from `format`:

```js
archiveCreator({ name: 'site.tar.gz' }); // tgz, from the extension
archiveCreator({ name: 'releases/site', format: 'tgz' }); // releases/site.tar.gz
archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip', archiverOptions: { zlib: { level: 9 } } }); // passed to archiver
```

## Options

| Option            | Type                      | Default     | Description                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`            | `string`                  | `'archive'` | The archive's path relative to the output folder: `site.zip`, `releases/site.tar.gz`. Without an extension the format's own is added. |
| `format`          | `'zip' \| 'tar' \| 'tgz'` | from `name` | Inferred from the extension of `name` (`.zip`, `.tar`, `.tgz`, `.tar.gz`), else zip.                                                  |
| `archiverOptions` | `ZipOptions & TarOptions` | —           | Passed to archiver: `zlib.level` or `store` for zip, `gzipOptions` for tgz. Must be an object (`Expected an object`).                 |
| `emptyArchive`    | `boolean`                 | `false`     | Emit an empty archive when the stream had no files. By default nothing is emitted.                                                    |
| `directories`     | `boolean`                 | `false`     | Add an entry for each directory in the stream (`src('**')` without `nodir`).                                                          |

All options are optional, and unknown keys are an error. `name` must stay inside the output folder: an absolute path or one that leaves it, such as `'../site.zip'`, is an error (`Expected a path inside the output folder`). Options are checked when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `ArchiveCreatorOptions`, `ArchiveFormat` and `ArchiverOptions`.

## Notes

* Read files with `src(…, { encoding: false })`: gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default, which breaks images, fonts and other binary files.
* The archive is placed relative to the `base` of the first file, so `dest('releases')` writes `releases/site.zip`.
* An explicit `format` wins over the extension, and the name is then kept as it is: `{ name: 'a.zip', format: 'tar' }` writes a tar named `a.zip`. Extensions are matched case-insensitively.
* Files read with `buffer: false` are archived from their stream.
* Files without contents that are not directories (`read: false`, symbolic links) are skipped. Directories are skipped too unless `directories` is set. With `directories`, the base folder itself (`src('dist')` matches `dist` with an empty relative path) gets no entry, since it has no path inside the archive.
* An error while reading streamed contents, or an error from archiver, fails the task with a `PluginError` named after this plugin; it is reported on the next file or at the end of the stream, and the process does not crash. archiver's warnings (a missing file, for example) fail the archive the same way rather than being ignored. After a failure, archiver is aborted, so the remaining entries are not read.
* An empty stream emits nothing unless `emptyArchive` is set; the empty archive is then named relative to the current folder.

## Migrating from 1.x

* Options are flat: `{ name, format, archiverOptions, emptyArchive, directories }` instead of `format`, `archiveOptions` and `pluginOptions: { archiveName, createDirectory, createEmptyArchive }`.
* `format` is no longer required: it is inferred from the extension of `name`.
* tar.gz (`tgz`) is supported.
* archiver 8 is used, streamed contents are supported and entries keep their modification time and mode.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/conditional.md
---
# conditional

Sends each file through the first branch whose condition holds for it, like if / else if / else for streams. A branch is any plugin or chain of plugins; files that no condition matches go to a default branch or pass through untouched.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-conditional
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';
import htmlSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-html-squeezer';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';

export const build = () =>
  src('src/**')
    .pipe(
      conditional({
        handlers: [
          { condition: ({ file }) => file.extname === '.js', handler: () => jsSqueezer() },
          { condition: ({ file }) => file.extname === '.html', handler: () => htmlSqueezer() }
        ]
      })
    )
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

A condition is a boolean or a function that gets `{ file }`, and a function may be async:

```js
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';
import refilename from '@zilero/gulp-refilename';
import { stat } from 'node:fs/promises';

conditional({
  handlers: [
    // a boolean: in development every file goes here
    { condition: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production', handler: () => refilename({ suffix: '.dev' }) },
    // an async function of the file
    { condition: async ({ file }) => (await stat(file.path)).size > 50_000, handler: () => jsSqueezer() }
  ],
  // everything else
  defaultHandler: () => refilename({ suffix: '.min' })
});
```

A handler may return an array of streams. They form a chain: the files go through them in order, and an error from any stream of the chain is emitted.

```js
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';
import cssSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer';
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

conditional({
  handlers: [{ condition: ({ file }) => file.extname === '.scss', handler: () => [scssCompiler(), cssSqueezer()] }]
});
```

Return an array, not `a().pipe(b())`. `.pipe()` returns its argument, so the handler would hand back `b` alone: the files would be written into `b` and skip `a`, and an error from `a` would not reach the task.

## Options

| Option           | Type                       | Default | Description                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `handlers`       | `{ condition, handler }[]` | none    | Branches, checked in order for every file; the first one whose condition holds gets it. At least one is required. |
| `defaultHandler` | `() => Duplex \| Duplex[]` | none    | Creates the stream, or the chain, for the files no condition matched. Without it they pass through untouched.     |

Each branch in `handlers`:

| Key         | Type                                                   | Description                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `condition` | `boolean \| ({ file }) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | `true`, or a function that returns `true`, sends the file here.                                           |
| `handler`   | `() => Duplex \| Duplex[]`                             | Creates the stream the matching files go through, or a non-empty array of streams to go through in order. |

Unknown keys are an error, and so are an empty `handlers` array (`Add at least one handler`) and a condition that is neither a boolean nor a function. Options are checked when the plugin is created. A handler that returns an empty array emits an error when its first file arrives (`A handler returned an empty array; return at least one stream`).

The package also exports the types `ConditionalOptions`, `ConditionalBranch`, `Condition`, `BranchHandler` and `BranchStream`.

## Notes

* Conditions are checked for every file, in the order of `handlers`; later conditions are not called once one holds.
* Each branch is created once, for the first file that goes to it. A branch that gets no files is never created.
* The stream ends after every branch has finished, so branches that emit files when they end (a concat or a bundle) work.
* Branches run side by side: files from different branches can come out in a different order than they went in.
* A slow branch slows the stream down: files wait until the branch can take more.
* A branch's output is not throttled by the downstream: what it emits is pushed on at once. A branch that emits a very large number of files, or very large ones, can hold them all in memory while a slow downstream catches up.
* A thrown condition fails the task with a `PluginError` named after this plugin.
* An error from a branch is reported on the next file written to the conditional stream, or at the end of the stream. A branch that fails while a condition is being awaited fails the stream too, instead of leaving it hanging. A `PluginError` keeps the name of the plugin that threw it, and any other error is wrapped in a `PluginError` named after this plugin when it happens, so it is not attributed to the file processed next.
* When the conditional ends, fails or is destroyed, every branch stream is destroyed with it, so no branch (a Sass compiler, for example) keeps the process alive.
* Every file goes through the conditions, including files without contents and directories.

## Migrating from 1.x

* Conditions are now checked for every file. In 1.x a condition was evaluated once when the plugin was created, and the whole stream went to one handler.
* A condition may be a function of the file (`({ file }) => …`), sync or async, as well as a boolean.
* A handler may return an array of streams to chain.
* Branches are created only when a file goes to them, and files that match nothing pass through when there is no `defaultHandler`.
* Files from different branches may interleave.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/file-exclude.md
---
# file-exclude

Drops files from the stream: those that match a glob or regular expression, fall outside a size range or that your own check rejects. Every other file passes through untouched.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-file-exclude
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import fileExclude from '@zilero/gulp-file-exclude';

export const copy = () =>
  src('src/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(fileExclude({ patterns: ['*.map', 'drafts/**'], size: { max: 1024 * 1024 } }))
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

The rules can be combined; a file is dropped as soon as one of them matches:

```js
fileExclude({ patterns: '*.map' }); // every source map, in any folder
fileExclude({ patterns: [/^drafts\//, /\.psd$/] }); // regular expressions on the relative path
fileExclude({ size: { min: 1 } }); // empty files
fileExclude({ exclude: ({ file }) => file.stem.startsWith('_') }); // your own check
```

## Options

| Option     | Type                                        | Default | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `patterns` | `string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]`  | none    | Globs (picomatch) or regular expressions matched against the path relative to `file.base`. An array needs at least one pattern.      |
| `size`     | `{ min?: number, max?: number }`            | none    | Drops files smaller than `min` or larger than `max` bytes. Both are non-negative integers, and `min` must not be greater than `max`. |
| `exclude`  | `({ file }) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | none    | Your own check, run after `patterns` and `size`: it gets one object with the Vinyl `file`; return `true` to drop the file.           |

Set at least one of them: options that exclude nothing are an error (`Set at least one of patterns, size or exclude`), and so is an empty `patterns` array (`Add at least one pattern`) or an empty glob. Unknown keys are an error too. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

Some globs are rejected rather than matched in a way you might not expect:

| Glob                       | Error                                                         | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `'!*.css'`                 | `Negated globs are not supported: list what to drop`          | In gulp-filter a `!` glob means "keep", here every pattern means "drop". List the files to drop instead, or use `exclude` to drop everything except some files: `({ file }) => !file.path.endsWith('.css')`. |
| `'drafts\\**'`             | `Expected / in globs, not \`                                  | Paths are matched with `/` separators on every platform, and `\` in a glob is an escape, so a Windows-style glob would never match.                                                                          |
| `'/home/me/src/drafts/**'` | `Expected a glob relative to file.base, not an absolute path` | Patterns are matched against `file.relative`, so an absolute glob would never match. Write it relative to the glob base of `src()`: `'drafts/**'`.                                                           |

Regular expressions are not checked this way: they are tested as they are.

The package also exports the types `FileExcludeOptions`, `ExcludePredicate` and `SizeRange`.

## Notes

* Paths use `/` separators on every platform, so the same patterns work on Windows.
* A glob without a slash matches the file name in any folder: `*.map` drops `app.js.map` and `js/vendor.js.map`. A glob with a slash matches the whole relative path: `drafts/**`, `img/*.png`.
* Globs match dotfiles: `img/*.png` also drops `img/.hidden.png`.
* Regular expressions are tested against the relative path, not only the name: use `/\.png$/` or `/^drafts\//`. A global (`g`) or sticky (`y`) RegExp works too: its `lastIndex` is reset before every file, so each test starts at the beginning of the path.
* `size` uses the length of the contents, or the size on disk (`file.stat.size`) for files without Buffer contents (`read: false`, streamed contents). Directories are never dropped by `size`, and neither are files of unknown size (no contents and no `stat`).
* The rules run in order (patterns, size, then `exclude`), so `exclude` only sees the files the first two kept.

## Migrating from 1.x

* A string in `patterns` is now a glob on the relative path, not a substring of the file name: replace `'.map'` with `'*.map'`.
* `size` is now `{ min, max }` instead of a `[min, max]` tuple; either bound can be left out.
* `onExclude` is renamed `exclude`; it gets `{ file }` instead of the file, and it may return a boolean as well as a promise.
* At least one rule is required.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/file-changed.md
---
# file-changed

Lets through only the files that changed since the last build: the built file in the destination is missing, older or different. Put it right after `src` so a watch build skips the rest of the pipeline for untouched files.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-file-changed
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import fileChanged from '@zilero/gulp-file-changed';
import imageSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-image-squeezer';

export const images = () =>
  src('src/images/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(fileChanged({ dest: 'dist/images' }))
    .pipe(imageSqueezer())
    .pipe(dest('dist/images'));
```

When the build renames files, tell the plugin where the built file is:

```js
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist/css', extname: '.css' }); // main.scss → dist/css/main.css
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: ({ file }) => `images/${file.stem}-1280w.jpg` }); // any other name
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', compare: 'contents' }); // for builds that copy files as they are
```

## Options

| Option    | Type                                                     | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dest`    | `string \| ({ file }) => string`                         | —         | The folder `dest` writes to, relative to `file.cwd` or absolute: the same value, or a function of the file. Required.                              |
| `extname` | `string`                                                 | —         | The extension the built file has, when the build changes it: `.css` for `.scss` sources. With its dot: `'css'` is an error.                        |
| `target`  | `({ file }) => string`                                   | —         | The built file's path, relative to `dest` or absolute, for builds that rename files in other ways. Wins over `extname`: `extname` is then ignored. |
| `compare` | `'mtime' \| 'contents' \| ({ file, target }) => boolean` | `'mtime'` | How a file counts as changed. See below.                                                                                                           |

`dest` and `target` are called once per file and must return a string, not a promise. `target` gets one object with the Vinyl `file`; a relative path it returns is resolved against `dest`, and an absolute one is used as it is:

```js
import path from 'node:path';

fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: ({ file }) => `pages/${file.stem}/index.html` }); // dist/pages/about/index.html
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: ({ file }) => path.resolve('cache', `${file.stem}.json`) }); // outside dest
```

`compare` can be:

| Value        | A file is changed when                                                                     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `'mtime'`    | It is newer than the built file, in whole milliseconds.                                    |
| `'contents'` | Its bytes differ from the built file.                                                      |
| a function   | It returns `true` (or a promise of `true`); it gets the file and `target: { path, stat }`. |

Unknown keys are an error. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `FileChangedOptions`, `CompareFunction`, `CompareInput`, `CompareMode`, `DestResolver` and `TargetResolver`.

## Notes

* Without `extname` or `target`, the built file is `dest` plus the path relative to `file.base`: `src/css/main.css` with `dest: 'dist'` is compared with `dist/css/main.css`.
* Files that were never built always pass, and so do directories.
* `'mtime'` compares whole milliseconds: `dest` writes modification times with millisecond precision, so the sub-millisecond fraction a source keeps would otherwise make every file look newer than its built copy.
* With `'mtime'`, files without a `stat` always pass. With `'contents'`, files without buffered contents (`buffer: false`, `read: false`) always pass.
* Files that did not change are dropped; the others pass through untouched.
* Only a missing built file counts as never built. Any other error while checking it, such as a permission error, fails the task with a `PluginError`; so does an error thrown by a `dest`, `target` or `compare` function.
* Not for plugins that combine files (concat, archives): they need every file, not only the changed ones.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/folder-clone.md
---
# folder-clone

Copies every file of the stream into one or more extra folders, relative to `file.base`, so a single `dest` writes them all. The originals are kept unless you turn them off, and a hook can change, replace or skip each copy.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-folder-clone
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import folderClone from '@zilero/gulp-folder-clone';

// dist/images/logo.png, dist/backup/images/logo.png and dist/v2/images/logo.png
export const images = () =>
  src('src/images/**', { base: 'src', encoding: false })
    .pipe(folderClone({ dirs: ['backup', 'v2'] }))
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

`onClone` runs for every copy:

```js
folderClone({
  dirs: ['legacy', 'drafts'],
  onClone: ({ file, dir, original }) => {
    if (dir === 'drafts') return null; // skip this copy
    file.stem = `${file.stem}-${dir}`; // change it in place
  }
});
```

## Options

| Option         | Type                                                 | Default | Description                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dirs`         | `string \| string[]`                                 | —       | One or more folders inside `file.base` that receive a copy of every file. Required. |
| `keepOriginal` | `boolean`                                            | `true`  | Emit the original file as well as the copies.                                       |
| `onClone`      | `({ file, dir, original }) => Vinyl \| null \| void` | —       | Runs for every copy, may be async. See below.                                       |

`onClone` gets:

| Key        | Description                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `file`     | The copy, already moved into `dir`; change it in place. |
| `dir`      | The folder this copy goes to, as given in `dirs`.       |
| `original` | The file the copy was made from.                        |

Return nothing to keep the copy, `null` to skip it, or another Vinyl file to emit instead.

Each folder in `dirs` must be a relative path inside `file.base`: an absolute path, `'.'` (the base itself), a path that leaves the base such as `'../out'`, and an empty string are errors, and so is an empty `dirs` list (`Add at least one folder`). Unknown keys are an error too. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `FolderCloneOptions`, `CloneHook` and `CloneInput`.

## Notes

* A copy keeps the original's `base` and gets the path `base/dir/relative`: `img/logo.png` with `dirs: 'backup'` becomes `backup/img/logo.png`.
* Copies are deep clones: each has its own contents and its own source map object, so changing a copy never touches the original or another copy.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, each copy's `sourceMap.file` points at the copy's relative path; the original's map is left as it was.
* For each file the original comes first, then one copy per folder in the order of `dirs`. With `keepOriginal: false` and every copy skipped, nothing is emitted for that file.
* Every file is cloned, including files without contents (`read: false`) and directories.
* Read images and other binary files with `src(…, { encoding: false })`; gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default.

## Migrating from 1.x

* 1.x only had an `onBeforeCopy(file)` hook and passed files through unchanged. 2.0 really copies each file into the folders in `dirs`.
* `keepOriginal` (default `true`) is new.
* `onBeforeCopy` is replaced by `onClone({ file, dir, original })`, which can change, replace or skip (`null`) each copy.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/reference/factory.md
---
# Plugin factory

`@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory` — the toolkit every plugin of the hub is built with. A guided tour is in [Writing a plugin](/guide/writing-plugins).

```ts
import {
  applySourceMap,
  assertBinaryContents,
  createPlugin,
  getChainableSourceMap,
  getInputSourceMap,
  isFunction,
  isRelativePathInside,
  parseOptions,
  PluginError,
  toPluginError,
  toPosixPath,
  Vinyl
} from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
```

## `createPlugin(definition)`

Returns an object-mode `Transform` stream: Vinyl files in, Vinyl files out, one at a time and in order.

| Field       | Type                                                             | Description                                                                                                |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`      | `string`                                                         | Prefixes every error; use the package name.                                                                |
| `accept`    | `'buffer' \| 'any'`                                              | `'buffer'` (default): `transform` gets files with Buffer contents only. `'any'`: every file.               |
| `filter`    | `(file: Vinyl) => boolean`                                       | Files it returns false for pass through untouched, before any other check.                                 |
| `transform` | `(file, context) => TransformResult \| Promise<TransformResult>` | Called for each file. Nothing: the file goes on. `null`: dropped. A file or an array: those go on instead. |
| `flush`     | `(context) => void \| Promise<void>`                             | Runs once after the last file, before the stream ends.                                                     |

`context` is `{ name, push }`: `push(file)` sends a file downstream from `transform` or `flush`.

A `filter` that throws is reported like any other error. With `accept: 'buffer'`, a file without contents passes through and a file with streamed contents emits `Streaming is not supported`. Anything `transform` or `flush` throws or rejects with is emitted as a `PluginError` with the plugin name and the file path (`fileName`); a `PluginError` is emitted as it is.

Types: `PluginDefinition`, `BufferPluginDefinition`, `AnyPluginDefinition`, `PluginContext`, `TransformResult`, `BufferFile` (a Vinyl file whose `contents` is a `Buffer`), `PluginStream`.

## `parseOptions({ name, schema, options })`

Validates `options` against a synchronous [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) (zod 4, valibot, arktype, …) and returns the parsed value, defaults applied. Invalid options throw a `PluginError`:

```text
Invalid options:
    • quality: Too big: expected number to be <=100
    • Unrecognized key: "qualty"
```

An asynchronous schema throws `The options schema must be synchronous`.

## `applySourceMap({ file, map, chain? })`

Stores a tool's source map (an object or JSON) as `file.sourceMap`, the way `dest(…, { sourcemaps })` expects it: `file` becomes the file's relative path, absolute or `file://` sources become relative to `file.base`, and every source uses `/`. With `chain: true` the file's current map is chained into the new one first, for tools that cannot take an input map; the new map's only source must be the file itself.

## `getChainableSourceMap(file)`

The file's map with absolute sources (`sourceRoot` applied), ready to chain into another map with `@jridgewell/remapping`; gulp keeps sources relative to `file.base`, while remapping resolves them against the map they are chained into. `undefined` when there is nothing to chain.

## `getInputSourceMap(file)`

The file's current map as JSON, to pass to a tool as its input map. `undefined` when the file has none, or has the empty map `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })` gives files without one: chaining that would leave the output map empty.

## `assertBinaryContents({ relative, contents })`

Throws when binary contents look like they were decoded as UTF-8 (the U+FFFD replacement character in the first 64 bytes), with the fix in the message: `` Read binary files with `src(globs, { encoding: false })` ``.

## `isFunction(value)`

A type guard for option schemas: `z.custom<Hook>(isFunction, 'Expected a function')` checks a callback without wrapping it.

## `isRelativePathInside(value)`

For option schemas: a relative path that stays inside the folder it is relative to and is not that folder. `css/main.css` passes; `/tmp/x`, `../x` and `.` do not.

## `toPosixPath(value)`

A path with `/` separators on every OS, for globs, archive entries, manifests and source maps.

## `toPluginError({ name, error, file? })`

Wraps anything in a `PluginError` prefixed with `name`, with `fileName` from the file; a `PluginError` is returned as it is. `createPlugin` uses it for every error.

## Types

* `ContentHook` — `(input: { content: string; file: Vinyl }) => string | Promise<string>`, the hook on a file's text the plugins share.
* `SourceMap`, `BufferFile`, `PluginDefinition`, `PluginContext`, `TransformResult`, `PluginStream`.

## Re-exports

* `PluginError` — the class from [plugin-error](https://github.com/gulpjs/plugin-error).
* `Vinyl` — the file class from [vinyl](https://github.com/gulpjs/vinyl), and its type: `import type { Vinyl } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory'`.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/reference/testing.md
---
# Testing helpers

`@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing` runs a plugin without gulp, for Vitest, Jest or `node:test`.

```ts
import { createFile, getContents, getRelativePath, runPlugin } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing';
```

## `createFile(input?)`

Creates a Vinyl file the way `gulp.src` would.

| Field       | Type                                                | Default      | Description                                                        |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`      | `string`                                            | `'file.txt'` | Path relative to `base`.                                           |
| `contents`  | `string \| Buffer \| NodeJS.ReadableStream \| null` | `''`         | A string is stored as UTF-8; `null` makes a file without contents. |
| `cwd`       | `string`                                            | `'/project'` |                                                                    |
| `base`      | `string`                                            | `<cwd>/src`  |                                                                    |
| `sourceMap` | `boolean`                                           | `false`      | Starts an empty map, like `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`.          |

## `runPlugin(stream, files)`

Writes the files into the stream, ends it and resolves with every file it emitted, in order. Rejects with the first error the stream emits.

```ts
const output = await runPlugin(refilename({ suffix: '.min' }), [createFile({ path: 'app.js' })]);
```

## `getContents(file)`

The Buffer contents of an emitted file. Throws when the file is missing or has no Buffer contents, so tests need no casts or non-null assertions on `contents`.

## `getRelativePath(file)`

The file's path relative to its base with `/` separators, so a test compares the same string on Linux, macOS and Windows:

```ts
expect(output.map(getRelativePath)).toEqual(['js/app.min.js']);
```
